requirements.requirement: The system must detect when the scoring engine returns an insufficiency response object instead of a score.
The system must propagate the insufficiency response from the scoring engine through the evaluate_care_facade without modification to its schema.
The system must prevent any numeric score field from being included in the facade response when an insufficiency response is returned.
The system must return a structured response containing valid_measure_count, required_minimum, missing_measure_types, and message fields when insufficiency is detected.
The system must ensure downstream consumers receive a consistent response type regardless of whether scoring succeeded or failed due to insufficiency.
The system must map both provider and clinical trial scoring outputs into the same facade-level insufficiency response contract.
The system must not attempt to compute or infer a fallback score when fewer than 3 valid measures are present.
The system must log an insufficiency event at the facade level including valid_measure_count and missing_measure_types.
The system must pass through a valid score response unchanged when the scoring engine returns a result with at least 3 valid measures.
The system must include a discriminator field or equivalent indicator in the facade response to distinguish between score and insufficiency outcomes.
The system must handle null or malformed scoring engine responses by returning a structured insufficiency response instead of propagating an error.
The system must handle unexpected exceptions from the scoring engine by returning a structured insufficiency response with a generic message.
The system must ensure no partial measure data or intermediate scoring values are exposed in the facade response when insufficiency is triggered.
The system must maintain backward-compatible response keys for downstream consumers when integrating insufficiency handling.
